title: Let Custom Branding replace app icons with custom SVGs
summary: Custom Branding gets a new **Icons** page where you can upload your own SVG pictures to replace eight app icons: Books, Search, Today, Saves, Bookmarks, Share, Chat and Discover. Uploaded icons are drawn as a single solid shape in the theme's icon color, so they change color in dark mode and when a button is active, just like the built-in icons. Anyone who opens the branding's share link should see the same custom icons.

links.label: Google Fonts icon library (download free SVG icons for testing)

setup.title: Open the preview build
setup.body: Open the preview link above in Chrome, Edge, Firefox or Safari on a computer. If the page shows an error or doesn't load, the build may still be deploying: wait a few minutes and reload. If the app looks like an older version, do a hard refresh: Ctrl+Shift+R on Windows, or Cmd+Shift+R on Mac.

setup.title: Sign in
setup.body: Custom Branding needs an account. Sign in with your email address; Seed Bible emails you a code, so use an inbox you can check.

setup.title: Download a few SVG icons
setup.body: Go to https://fonts.google.com/icons. Click any icon (for example **Favorite**, the heart), and in the panel that opens choose **SVG** to download it. Download three different ones, such as **Favorite** (heart), **Home** and **Pets** (paw). Note which is which, since you'll check that each shows up in the right place. Also have any ordinary photo or `.png` / `.jpg` picture ready for one test.

setup.title: Open a Custom Branding editor
setup.body: Open your **Profile** (click your round profile picture in the sidebar), then choose **Your content**. Either open an existing branding card, or choose **Create** → **Custom Branding** to make a new one. The customization editor opens beside the reader. While the editor is open, the reader already shows your branding, so you can see icon changes right away.

tests.title: The editor has an Icons row that opens a list of the eight icons
steps: In the customization editor, scroll down below the **Themes** list.
Find the **Icons** row and look at the small text under it.
Click the **Icons** row.
expected: The **Icons** row says "0 of 8 customized" (if this branding has no custom icons yet).
A page titled **Icons** opens with the text "Upload an SVG to replace any of these icons. Icons are drawn as a single shape in the theme's icon color."
It lists eight rows, in this order: **Books**, **Search**, **Today**, **Saves**, **Bookmarks**, **Share**, **Chat**, **Discover**.
Each row shows a small preview of the app's current icon on the left and an **Upload SVG** button on the right.

tests.title: Uploading an SVG replaces the preview and the icon in the app
steps: On the **Icons** page, click **Upload SVG** on the **Search** row.
Pick the heart SVG you downloaded.
expected: After a moment, the **Search** row's preview shows the heart.
The **Search** row's button now says **Replace**, and a small **X** button appears next to it.
In the reader's toolbar, the Search button (normally a magnifying glass) now shows the heart, in the same color as the other toolbar icons (not black, unless the other icons are black).

tests.title: The Icons row counts how many icons are customized
tests.before: You uploaded the Search icon in the previous test.
steps: Upload the **Home** SVG for **Books** and the **Pets** (paw) SVG for **Today**.
Go back to the main editor page (the back arrow at the top of the editor).
expected: The **Icons** row now says "3 of 8 customized".

tests.title: Replace swaps in a different SVG
steps: Open the **Icons** page again.
On the **Search** row, click **Replace** and pick the **Pets** (paw) SVG.
expected: The **Search** preview changes from the heart to the paw.
The Search button in the reader now shows the paw.

tests.title: The X button brings back the app's own icon
steps: On the **Search** row, hover over the **X** button and read the tooltip, then click it.
expected: The tooltip says "Use the default Search icon".
The **Search** preview goes back to the magnifying glass, and the button says **Upload SVG** again with no **X**.
The reader's Search button shows the magnifying glass again.

tests.title: A file that isn't an SVG is turned away with a message
steps: On the **Share** row, click **Upload SVG**.
In the file picker, switch the file type filter to **All files** if needed, and pick a `.png` or `.jpg` picture.
expected: A message appears: "Icons must be SVG files."
The **Share** preview still shows the app's own share icon, and the button still says **Upload SVG**.

sections.title: Where the custom icons show up
sections.intro: Each icon should change everywhere that button appears, not just in one spot.

setup.title: Customize all eight icons
setup.body: On the **Icons** page, upload an SVG for every row. Reusing the same three SVGs is fine, but remember which you used where. The Icons row should end up saying "8 of 8 customized".

tests.title: Computer-width screen: every customized icon appears in the reader
steps: With the browser window wide, look at the reader's toolbar and header buttons, and the sidebar.
Find each of: the Books button (normally the Seed Bible seed logo that opens the book picker), Search, Today, Saves (star), Bookmarks, Share and Discover (compass).
If you have a chat available, also find the Chat button (speech bubble).
expected: Each of those buttons shows the SVG you uploaded for it instead of the app's own icon.
All custom icons are about the same size as the built-in icons around them, and none are cut off, stretched or blurry.
They're drawn in the same color as the nearby built-in icons.

tests.title: The Share item in a tab's menu uses the custom Share icon
steps: Open the menu on the current reading tab (the tab's options in the header), and look at the **Share** item.
expected: The **Share** item shows your custom Share SVG at a small size that lines up with the other menu item icons.

tests.title: Active and hover states still change the custom icon's color
steps: Hover the mouse over a custom toolbar icon, such as Saves or Bookmarks.
Click **Saves** (the star button) to turn on the saves filter, then click it again to turn it off.
Click **Bookmarks** to open the bookmarks panel, then close it.
expected: The custom icons change color when hovered or turned on, the same way the built-in icons do.

Note for testers: the built-in Saves star and Bookmarks icons fill in when turned on. A custom icon stays the same shape and only changes color; that's expected, since one SVG is used for both states.

tests.title: Phone-width screen: the bottom tabs use the custom icons
steps: Make the browser window narrow, about the width of a phone, until a bar of tabs appears at the bottom. (Or open the preview on a phone, signed in to the same account with the editor open.)
Look at the **Today**, **Bible** and **Search** tabs at the bottom.
Open the **More** menu, if there is one, and look at **Bookmarks**.
expected: The **Today**, **Bible** (uses the Books icon) and **Search** tabs show your custom SVGs.
The selected tab's icon is highlighted in the same way as before.
**Bookmarks** in the More menu shows your custom Bookmarks SVG.

tests.title: Custom icons follow dark mode
steps: Open **Settings** → **Display & Theme** and switch to the dark theme (or switch your branding to a dark theme).
expected: The custom icons switch to the light icon color used in dark mode, and stay easy to see against the dark background, just like the built-in icons.

tests.title: Custom icons are still there after a reload
steps: Reload the page (Ctrl+R on Windows, Cmd+R on Mac).
Open the same branding from **Your content** again and open the **Icons** page.
expected: All your uploaded icons are still listed with their previews, and "8 of 8 customized" shows on the Icons row.
The reader shows the custom icons again while the editor is open.

tests.title: Someone who opens the share link sees the custom icons
steps: On the main editor page, click **Share** at the bottom. A message says the link was copied.
Open a private/incognito window and paste the link into its address bar. Don't sign in.
expected: The app opens with your branding, and the buttons you customized show your SVGs instead of the app's own icons.

tests.title: Removing an icon also removes it for people using the share link
steps: Back in your signed-in window, on the **Icons** page, click the **X** on the **Today** row.
In the private window, reload the page.
expected: In the private window, the Today button now shows the app's own Today icon, while the other custom icons are still there.

sections.title: Things that should not have changed

tests.title: Without custom icons, every icon looks as it did before
steps: Close the customization editor so no branding is active (or use a private window with the plain preview link, without the share link).
Look at the Books (seed logo), Search, Today, Saves, Bookmarks, Share, Chat and Discover buttons at computer width and phone width.
expected: They all show the app's own icons, at the same size and position as on the live site. The seed logo still animates where it used to.
Saves still fills in its star when turned on, and Bookmarks still changes when its panel is open.

tests.title: The logo upload in the editor still works
steps: In the customization editor's main page, use the **Logo** area to upload or replace the logo with any picture.
Crop it and choose **Set logo**.
expected: The logo updates as before. Uploading icons didn't change how the logo works.

notCovered: The "That SVG is too large" message for files over 256 KB. Real icon files are almost never that big, and the size check is covered by automated tests.
A branding made by a newer version of the app that replaces icons this version doesn't know about. The app should just ignore those; that's covered by automated tests.
Rejecting icon links that aren't normal web addresses, a safety check covered by automated tests.
